task.description: WF-02 Step 1b -- hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's REQ-075 design. Independently re-verified every load-bearing R-Co source claim against the actual files (not the design doc's word) given this is the highest-risk requirement in the batch: global tenants table, no REQ-072 prefix scoping, PLATFORM_ADMIN role check as the only protection.
acceptance_criteria: listing tenants as a non-PLATFORM_ADMIN caller returns 403 and no tenant data whatsoever, including no count and no total, demonstrated by asserting the full response body

reading, patching, deactivating and reactivating another tenant's record as a caller authenticated for a different tenant is rejected, with each of the four verbs covered by its own test and each verified to leave the target tenant's row unchanged (INV-1)
the moduledoc states R-Co's actual rule on whether a tenant admin may read or patch their own tenant record, and a test covers that rule in both the allowed and denied direction

tenant creation routes to Letflow.TenantProvisioning and results in a provisioned schema with REQ-022's migrations replayed, demonstrated by querying information_schema for a table in the new schema -- not by trusting the 201

a deactivated tenant's subsequent authenticated request receives a response consistent with Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus's behaviour, with the expected status named in the moduledoc and asserted by a test

the moduledoc states explicitly that these handlers operate outside REQ-072's per-tenant prefix scoping, names PLATFORM_ADMIN as the only protection, and explains why that makes this group higher-risk than the rest of S4
the moduledoc states how handleCreateTenant relates to REQ-076's onboarding endpoint, so the platform has one provisioning path rather than two

result.summary: Independently re-read every cited R-Co source location, not just the design's claims. (1) AC3: read src/identity/service.zig L110-568 directly -- getTenantAdmin (505-521), patchTenant (523-568+), createTenant (445-470), listTenantsAdmin (490-503), applyTenantLifecycleAction (110-131) each open with a bare `if (actor.role != .PLATFORM_ADMIN) return error.Forbidden` and none of the five bodies contains any subsequent target-tenant-vs-caller comparison -- design's claim confirmed exactly. (2) Section 1.2 dead-code finding: read main.zig's resource=='tenants' branch (1492-1541) and sibling resource=='users' branch (1447-1470) directly -- both construct `actor.role = .PLATFORM_ADMIN` unconditionally as a literal in the AuthContext, and user_id is read from the unauthenticated `X-Bpm-User-Id` header (main.zig ~302) defaulting to the all-zero UUID when absent -- confirmed exactly. The design's instruction not to port this and to derive the real role from the verified bearer token (conn.assigns.auth_context.roles) is stated unambiguously in prose, not merely implied. (3) Section 4.1: read service.zig:133-151 (enforceTenantActiveForOperation -- PLATFORM_ADMIN exempt, INACTIVE -> error.TenantInactive) and auth.zig:1663-1678 (checked on every authenticated request via authenticate/3, not gated to write methods; 403 tenant_inactive on non-exempt inactive-tenant callers) -- confirmed. Cross-checked against the actually-shipped lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex: write-methods-only (`@write_methods` guard on call/2's first clause), 503 status, no PLATFORM_ADMIN exemption, and lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex confirms the Ecto.Enum values list is exactly `[:active, :migrating]` (no :inactive) -- design's description of the shipped file is accurate. (4) Confirmed the design's refusal to implement Section 4.2 is an explicit, unambiguous blocking condition on ELIXIR-DEV ('Do not implement Section 4.2 without REVIEWER confirming this shape first'), not a passing mention -- correctly gates a behavior-contract change to an already-shipped REQ-021 module. (5) Read lib/letflow/api/response.ex's forbidden/2 -- takes (conn, detail :: String.t()), detail is entirely caller-chosen, no query-derived data can reach it structurally -- design's claim confirmed. (6) All 7 acceptance criteria are mapped to a distinct design section (AC1->1.3/6.2, AC2->5, AC3->3/2.1pt3, AC4->7.1, AC5->4/2.1pt5, AC6->2.1pt2, AC7->2.1pt4/7.1) -- none dropped or merged, each satisfied by a specific moduledoc-text requirement plus a concrete test design. (7) Read lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex directly: confirmed update_changeset/2 currently casts [:display_name, :status] together, so the design's flagged divergence (splitting into admin_patch_changeset/2 casting only [:display_name] and status_changeset/2 casting only [:status], so PATCH structurally cannot touch status and deactivate/reactivate structurally cannot touch display_name) is a real, correctly-identified gap, and the structural-impossibility-over-runtime-rejection reasoning matches this same module's own established idp_realm_id-immutability idiom. (8) No implementation code present: the only literal Elixir snippets are one-line endpoint_policy_key/2 pattern-match clauses, which is the identical established convention already used and passed in REQ-073's design (verified by grep against lib/letflow/design/req073-identity-user-routes.md, which uses the exact same clause-per-route style) -- not new implementation smuggled in. Everything else is @spec signatures, response/error shapes, and ExUnit test-spec sketches. (9) Read main.zig's route dispatch directly: resource=='tenants' (1492) and resource=='users' (1447) are both top-level sibling branches in the same if/else chain, not nested -- confirms the design's basis for a new sibling Letflow.Routers.Tenants module rather than nesting under Letflow.Routers.Identity. All load-bearing claims verified against primary source, not the design doc's paraphrase. No gaps found; no TBD/deferral language; every new function signature includes its full {:ok,_}|{:error,_} shape.
result.next_action: Route to ELIXIR-DEV (WF-02 Step 2a). Two conditions carried forward from CODE-DESIGNER's own handoff, both confirmed sound and both must remain binding: (a) Section 4.2's extension to Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus (adding an all-methods, PLATFORM_ADMIN-exempt, 403 tenant_inactive check ahead of the existing write-only :migrating check) must not be implemented until REVIEWER confirms the shape -- ELIXIR-DEV should implement AC1-AC4/AC6/AC7 and the non-Section-4.2 parts of AC5's moduledoc/test scaffolding first, or otherwise sequence a REVIEWER checkpoint before touching tenant_status.ex; (b) OQ-4 (oidc_mode source for create_tenant/1) and OQ-5 (no compensating rollback on partial provisioning failure) are pre-existing/accepted open questions, not blockers, but ELIXIR-DEV must not silently resolve them without noting the choice made.
